citeAs: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022).
creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan (University of California Los Angeles, Arizona State University, Allen Institute for AI)
description: ScienceQA is a large-scale multimodal multiple-choice science question answering benchmark consisting of 21,208 questions with diverse science topics spanning natural science, social science, and language science. Questions are sourced from elementary and high school science curricula (grades 1–12) and most are annotated with corresponding lectures and explanations that serve as chain-of-thought reasoning annotations. The dataset includes multimodal contexts (images and text) and covers 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills.
name: ScienceQA
publisher: University of California Los Angeles / Allen Institute for AI (AI2)
rai:annotationsPerItem: For the human performance study, each test question was answered by 3 different AMT workers. For human evaluation of generated explanations, each sample was evaluated by 3 AMT workers. 83.9% of questions are annotated with a lecture and 90.5% with an explanation.
rai:annotatorDemographics: For the human performance study on Amazon Mechanical Turk, only workers who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification examples were eligible. Workers needed to correctly answer 4 out of 5 exam examples to qualify.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human evaluation of generated explanations, human scores for each explanation were determined by taking a majority vote across 3 AMT workers. Workers rated explanations on relevance, correctness, and completeness. Results showed that 65.2% of GPT-3 (CoT) generated explanations met the gold standard (relevant, correct, and complete) by human evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for the human performance study and human evaluation of generated explanations. A custom data exploration tool was also developed for expert review (accessible at https://scienceqa.github.io/explore.html).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations. The lecture provides general knowledge introducing background information for solving problems of a similar class. The explanation reveals a specific reason for the answer. To ensure data quality, a data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts. The dataset was randomly split into training, validation, and test splits with a ratio of 60:20:20 (12,726 / 4,241 / 4,241 examples respectively).
rai:dataBiases: Blind studies showed that results from question-only and image-context-only inputs are close to random chance, indicating the dataset is robust and reliable in distribution. Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern, mitigating answer-position bias. The dataset is sourced from California Common Core Content Standards, which may introduce geographic and curriculum-specific biases.
rai:dataCollection: Questions in the ScienceQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted using heuristic rules. Invalid questions (those with only one choice, faulty data, or duplicates) were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled to ensure choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Science problems sourced from IXL Learning (https://www.ixl.com/), an online K-12 education platform. Raw data consisted of science problems aligned with California Common Core Content Standards, containing questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions.
rai:dataLimitations: Current multimodal models fail to achieve satisfactory performance on ScienceQA, with a 20.07% gap between human performance and the best model for image-context questions. Models using image captions lack fine-grained visual semantics and do not work well for diagrams. Large language models struggle with questions requiring complex domain-specific knowledge. The dataset is restricted to non-commercial research use only, with copyright belonging to IXL Learning.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from downloaded problems using heuristic rules. Invalid questions (only one choice, faulty data, duplicates) were manually removed. Answer options were shuffled to remove ordering patterns. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions so that special structures (tables, lists) are distinguishable from plain text. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples, and incorrect annotations were manually revised by experts.
rai:dataSocialImpact: ScienceQA collects science questions from textbooks and is proposed to diagnose multimodal understanding and multi-hop reasoning abilities of AI systems. The dataset does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race. After careful examination, no improper content (pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias) was found. The authors adhere to the goal of AI for the common good, and any anti-social data points will be removed based on feedback. The dataset is beneficial for K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems.
rai:dataUseCases: ScienceQA is intended as a benchmark for multimodal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence research. It is also intended to contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: A captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 (available at https://huggingface.co/nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) was used to generate captions for images in the dataset, with maximum caption length of 16, 4 beams, and maximum 512 output tokens. Sentence-BERT was used to compute cosine similarity of semantic embeddings for evaluating generated explanations.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain personally identifiable information or offensive content. It does not contain user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race.

null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe or date range for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not discuss missing data handling in the collection process; questions without context are handled by replacing context with an empty string, but this is an experimental detail not a collection gap.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol for missing values is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, balancing) is described for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
